list.title: Metrics
list.intro: Create event metrics directly with “New metric”, or save them from event analysis results (the full definition currently configured is included). Retention metrics are still created from retention analysis results. A metric can carry its own query time and value pick; alert rules follow the metric time range by default (they can override it in the rule — see Ops → Monitoring alerts → New metric alert). Click a display name to view the full definition; editing and deleting (with confirmation) both happen in the details drawer. The metric name and type cannot be changed (the identifier stays stable, so existing references and alert bindings are unaffected).

valuePick.extra: Empty = automatic (recommended by the calculation method); consistent with existing alert definitions

hint.sum: Sum of the daily values in the window; days without data count as 0
hint.avg: Sum of daily values divided by the number of days; days without data count as 0
hint.max: Largest daily value with data in the window
hint.min: Smallest daily value with data in the window
hint.weighted: Weighted by the denominator (the only correct form for per-user averages)
hint.lastDay: Value of the most recent day with data (often "today so far")
hint.firstDay: Value of the earliest day with data in the window
hint.uniqTotal: Evaluated over the whole window instead of summing per day (the only correct form for distinct counts)

note.sum: Sum of the daily values in the window; days without data count as 0
note.avg: Sum of daily values divided by the number of days in the window; days without data count as 0
note.max: Largest value among the days that have data in the window (no data at all → skipped this round)
note.min: Smallest value among the days that have data in the window (no data at all → skipped this round)
note.weighted: Weighted by the denominator (the only correct pick for per-user counts/values); evaluated over the whole range
note.lastDay: Value of the most recent day with data in the window (often used for "today so far")
note.firstDay: Value of the earliest day with data in the window
note.uniqTotal: Evaluated over the whole range instead of summing per day (the only correct pick for distinct counts / triggered users)

warning.nonAdditivePickedAdditive: This analysis method cannot be summed per day. Choose "Deduplicated total" or "Weighted average", otherwise the result will be too high.
warning.additivePickedOverall: This analysis method is additive, so "Cumulative" or "Daily average" reads better; a deduplicated total only makes sense for distinct-count or per-user methods.

window.fromDateToToday: From a chosen date to today
window.fromDateToYesterday: From a chosen date to yesterday

timeRange.extra: Once the metric carries its own time range, alert rules follow it by default; only relative ranges are supported (so they can be evaluated every day), up to 90 days

conditionGroup.extra: Event properties / user properties / cohorts / tags; same semantics as the condition group in event analysis

prop.eventDisabledPlaceholder: This method does not need a property
prop.tooltip: Required when the calculation method needs a property; the property type determines which methods are available

event.staleOption: {{event}} (not in the event list; keeping the current value)

transform.tooltip: Arithmetic is applied first, then the value is rounded to the given number of decimal places (same as event analysis)

trial.hint: Evaluates the current definition once against real data (same implementation as alert evaluation); nothing is saved

validation.metricNamePattern: Start with a lowercase letter; use only lowercase letters, digits and underscores; up to 80 characters

create.title: New event metric
create.displayNamePlaceholder: e.g. Average daily order amount over the last 7 days
create.metricNameExtra: Unique asset key; it cannot be changed after creation. Analyses and alerts reference the metric by it
create.definitionHint: Definition (same depth as event analysis; run a trial before saving)

modal.title: Create metric
modal.metricNameExtra: Start with a lowercase letter; may contain lowercase letters, digits and underscores; up to 80 characters
modal.summaryEventEmpty: Configure an event metric and run a query first
modal.summaryNote: . The time range is taken from the query and is not stored in the metric.

apply.empty: No saved metrics of this type

detail.title: Metric details
detail.readonlyNote: The metric name is the unique asset key and the type determines the definition model; changing either would break existing analysis and alert references, so both are read-only.
detail.alertBody: A metric can carry its own query time and value pick; when the query time is unset, alerts are evaluated over the rule window (existing behaviour). When a metric is applied to analysis, the analysis page uses its own time range. Editing the definition of a metric that alert rules reference also changes the alert condition (Ops → Monitoring alerts → Policies).
detail.retentionFiltersBody: Filter conditions attached to the start/return events are kept with the events; the cohort range and cycle can be adjusted here.
detail.cohortRangeTooltip: Time range of mature cohorts for retention; when unset it is derived from the cycle (≥ cycle + 1 day, up to 180 days)

message.cardCreated: Card “{{name}}” created; add it to a dashboard in the dashboard studio
message.noEventMetric: No event metric available to save

confirm.deleteEditing: The metric will be deleted and unsaved edits will be lost. Analyses and alerts referencing it will stop working.
confirm.deleteContent: Analyses and alerts referencing it will stop working; deletion cannot be undone.
